svg.title: HTTP first-business-event and event-delivery p95 latency
svg.desc: Two zero-baseline panels at the recorded reader counts. Blue circles are raw; orange diamonds are runtime. Each dot is a run p95 in milliseconds; at 1/4/8 reader observations the first-event p95 equals the slowest reader. Median lines and min-max whiskers summarize runs, not confidence intervals or tail-latency SLOs.

rect.style: stroke: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 1; fill: rgb(100%,100%,100%); fill-rule: evenodd;

g.text: 64 events/run | 128 ASCII message bytes (+ metadata) | SQLite WAL / NORMAL | 1 producer | localhost HTTP

circle.style: stroke: rgb(0%,44%,69%); stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 1.8; fill: rgb(100%,100%,100%); fill-rule: evenodd;

path.style: stroke: rgb(83%,36%,0%); stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 2.5; stroke-dasharray: 7, 4;

polygon.style: stroke: rgb(83%,36%,0%); stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-width: 1.8; fill: rgb(100%,100%,100%); fill-rule: evenodd;

g.text: Dots: 3 runs | line: median | whiskers: min-max (not CI)
Recorded 2026-10-18 | Apple M3 Pro | Python 3.11.10 | SQLite 3.54.0
Source: baseline-2026-10-18.json | input SHA256 and values: series.json

g.text: First event includes request setup and reader admission; delivery ends at complete client frame parsing.
At 1/4/8 readers, first-event p95 is the slowest reader. Each dot is one run; percentiles are never pooled.
